clue.text: Forgers use this very penetrating dye

indicators.note: one piece penetrating another is driven inside it

parts.note: anil is indigo, a blue dye

explanation.surface: A dye so strong it soaks deep into whatever it touches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forgers' are blacksmiths here, not counterfeiters.
explanation.definitionFit: Blacksmiths hammer hot metal on this iron block, so it is the tool forgers use.

clue.text: Desperate appeals to protect mother producing a lump in your throat

indicators.note: a protector wraps round what it guards, so the scrambled letters surround the next piece
desperate suggests wild, frantic disorder, so the letters of appeals are rearranged

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: Frantic pleas made to shield a mother leave you choked with emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desperate' rearranges the letters to AS APPLE, which 'to protect' splits open. 'A lump in your throat' sounds like emotion, but is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The larynx makes a visible bump at the front of the neck, especially in men.

clue.text: Energy's put into mounting television screen

indicators.note: one piece is put into the other, sitting inside it
in a down clue, mounting means climbing, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Fixing a power supply inside a wall-mounted TV screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounting' turns TV into VT; E goes into it. 'Screen' looks like part of the television, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen candidates is to check them carefully, which is what vetting does.

clue.text: Prince keeping model up quite long into the night

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the assembled letters read from the bottom
one piece keeping another holds it inside

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V
to sit for an artist is to model

explanation.surface: A prince keeps an artist's model awake until the small hours.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the whole assembly from the bottom, not just 'model'.
explanation.definitionFit: Latish means somewhat late, as an hour well into the evening is.

clue.text: It helps you see and escape predicament

parts.note: on the lam is American slang for escaping, so lam is an escape
a plight is a difficult situation

explanation.surface: Something that lights the way and gets you out of a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from a lamp is what allows the eyes to make things out in the dark.

clue.text: Abundant laughing follows some light fun, with sides splitting

indicators.note: follows places this piece after the ones before it

parts.note: the lux is a unit of illumination, an amount of light

indicators.note: a word whose sides split off loses its outer letters, leaving only the centre

parts.note: riant is a literary word for laughing

explanation.surface: Plenty of laughter after a bit of light-hearted fun, everyone splitting their sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With sides splitting' strips F and N from 'fun', leaving U.
explanation.definitionFit: Luxuriant growth is lush and plentiful, so the word means profuse or rich.

clue.text: Frantic bloke with ultimate responsibility?

parts.note: a bloke is a man
IC stands for in charge, the person with final responsibility

explanation.surface: The man where the buck stops is run off his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic behaviour is wildly energetic and agitated, much like frenzied activity.

clue.text: Revolutionary embraces English church, showing forbearance

indicators.note: something that embraces another wraps its arms round it

parts.note: Lenin led the Russian Revolution
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A revolutionary warmly welcomes the English church, displaying patience.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenience is mild tolerance of faults, which is what patient restraint amounts to.

clue.text: Resident picked up single friend, creating uninformed speculation

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a guest is someone staying, as at a hotel
I is the Roman numeral one
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A hotel resident collected a lone friend, which set tongues wagging.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is said 'guest-imate', so the GUESST part is how 'guest' sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A guesstimate is a rough estimate based mostly on conjecture rather than facts.

clue.text: Rank outsiders in race idiot backed

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the letters are reversed
the outsiders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: In a race, the rank outsiders were backed by some fool.
explanation.walkthrough: The outside letters RE and IT give REIT, which 'backed' reverses. 'Backed' and 'outsiders' are betting words here.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a level or row, as a rank is in a hierarchy.

clue.text: On vacation taipan in taxi somehow bites Oscar? He'll need one!

indicators.note: the scrambled letters bite into the next piece, holding it inside
somehow says the letters come out in some new order
a word on vacation is emptied of its insides, leaving only its ends

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A deadly snake loose in a taxi sinks its fangs into Oscar, who will need emergency treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges the pool to ANTITXIN, which 'bites' the O. A taipan is a deadly Australian snake, so the victim needs the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bitten by a venomous snake needs antivenom, a serum that counters toxins.

clue.text: One related delightful, entertaining tale finally

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: nice means pleasant or delightful

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A charming relative tells a lovely, entertaining story at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a family member, the daughter of a sibling.

clue.text: They're involved in court action to suppress dodgy businesses

parts.note: to squash a revolt is to suppress it
rackets are dishonest moneymaking schemes

explanation.surface: Legal proceedings aimed at shutting down crooked firms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court action' suggests a lawsuit; the court is a squash court.
explanation.definitionFit: Players hit the ball with these on an enclosed walled court.

clue.text: Completely engaged in joust outside hotel, what?

parts.note: to be up to something is to be busy doing it

indicators.note: one piece outside another surrounds it

parts.note: to tilt is to joust with a lance
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
eh is a questioning noise meaning what?

explanation.surface: A knight completely absorbed in jousting outside a hotel asks what's going on.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom refers to a blade thrust in as far as its handle, hence fully or totally.

clue.text: Presidential candidate consuming cold coffee and cheese

indicators.note: something consuming another swallows it whole, holding it inside

parts.note: Bob Dole ran for US president in 1996
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: A would-be president having a snack of iced coffee and cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolcelatte is a soft, mild Italian blue variety from Lombardy.

clue.text: Husband's upset about weight

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to tip something is to upset or overturn it

explanation.surface: A husband is upset about how heavy he has become.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weight' is not heaviness but importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Pith is the essential substance or significance of an argument, as weight is.

clue.text: Liqueur is to damage cloth when absorbed

indicators.note: absorbed means soaked up inside, so this piece goes within the others

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
chino is a cotton twill fabric
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A sticky liqueur will stain fabric once it soaks in.
explanation.definitionFit: Maraschino is a clear cherry-flavoured spirit made from marasca cherries.

clue.text: I worry that endlessly flying planes must be this

indicators.note: flying suggests letters scattered loose, so they are rearranged
endlessly drops the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A nervous flyer insists that aircraft must be safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' takes the T off 'that'; the letters of I WORRY THA are then reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft fit to fly is certified as such, which every working plane must be.

clue.text: App at last rightly designed for tablet

indicators.note: designed means freshly arranged, so the letters are reordered
at last picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An app properly designed at last for use on a tablet computer.
explanation.walkthrough: P from 'App' joins RIGHTLY to be rearranged. 'Tablet' is not a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A triglyph is a grooved block or panel in a Doric frieze, a carved slab in classical architecture.

clue.text: A volume from America, not the first of adult books?

parts.note: liter is the American spelling of litre, a unit of volume

indicators.note: not the first of means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: mature means grown-up or adult

explanation.surface: An American book that is not suitable for grown-ups?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' looks like a book, but here is a measure; 'adult books' suggests something racier.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature is written works collectively, the body of novels, poems and so on.

clue.text: Non-professional swimmer lacks training

indicators.note: lacks means is without, so some letters are taken out

parts.note: plaice is a flatfish, a swimmer
PE is physical education, school exercise training

explanation.surface: An amateur swimmer has had no coaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a person but is a fish; P and E are removed from either end.
explanation.definitionFit: Laic means of the laity, people outside a profession, especially the clergy.

clue.text: Moderate politician brought in to support Right

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside, so this piece sits within the other

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A moderate politician recruited to back the political right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' looks like an adjective but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to soften or tone it down.

clue.text: One's included in e.g. the Melrose dancing?

definitions.text: One's included in e.g. the Melrose dancing?

indicators.note: included in means put inside the other piece
dancing letters jump about into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Is this the sort of dance you'd see in the Scottish town of Melrose?
explanation.walkthrough: I goes into the letters of E.G. THE MELROSE, all rearranged by 'dancing'. Melrose is a Scottish Borders town, and the whole clue describes the Scottish dance.
explanation.definitionFit: This lively Scottish country dance for eight people would be danced in a Borders town.

clue.text: Section of orchestra should refuse

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the orchestra ought to decline to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse means rubbish or waste, the stuff thrown away.

clue.text: No room for lawyer's wig? Rubbish!

indicators.note: no ... for means there is none of this piece, so it is taken away

parts.note: the lawyer's wig is the shaggy ink cap, a fungus also called shaggy mane

explanation.surface: A barrister complains there's no space for a wig, then dismisses the complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: The lawyer's wig is a fungus, not courtroom headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: Mush is slang for sentimental nonsense, as rubbish can mean foolish talk.

clue.text: Being at one university's extremely trendy

indicators.note: extremely picks the letters at the extremes, the first and last

explanation.surface: A university is in total agreement that it is very fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Unity is the state of being united or in agreement.

clue.text: George wants gold given to religious group

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
pi is slang for pious, religious
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A man called George wants his gold passed to a sect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' is old pilots' slang for the automatic pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircrew nicknamed the automatic flight system George, as in 'let George fly it'.

clue.text: Support on stage

definitions.meaning: a table or chair stands on its supports
in cricket the on side is also called the ... side
a stage of a journey or race is one section of it

explanation.surface: Backing someone in a theatre performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: 'on' is the cricket term for the leg side of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Each word names one sense: a limb that holds up, a cricket side, and a section of a journey.

clue.text: Turn in those people importing heroin, acting on nameless tip

indicators.note: on places this piece after the one before it
nameless means without N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: a hint is a tip

indicators.note: importing means bringing inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: they means those people
H is slang for heroin
A is the abbreviation for acting, as in an acting rank

explanation.surface: Drug importers taking H act on an anonymous tip-off.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn in is an idiom for going to bed, as is the slang phrase for sleep.

clue.text: Irish accent gives away British villain

indicators.note: gives away means lets go of, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a brogue is a strong Irish accent

explanation.surface: A villain's Irish accent betrays that he is British.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest scoundrel.
